newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK GRAFT BUSTERS ARREST 18 MORE IN HORSE RACE SCANDAL.
newsitem.headline: HK GRAFT BUSTERS ARREST 18 MORE IN HORSE RACE SCANDAL.

text.p: Hong Kong's anti-corruption body said on Monday it had arrested 36 people in less than 24 hours over alleged illegal bookmaking and race fixing.
The Independent Commission Against Corruption (ICAC) said in a statement it had arrested a further 18 people since a similar number were seized at Sunday night's race meeting.

The 36 people who were arrested included five jockeys, two trainers and three Hong Kong Jockey Club staff, after Sunday's swoop which raided 55 premises and arrested 18 people, an ICAC spokeswoman told Reuters by telephone.
She said five people had been released on bail, while the remaining 31 were still being detained. No charges had been brought yet on the 36.
The spokeswoman declined to give further details on the probe, saying inquiries were continuing.

Hong Kong is Asia's biggest horseracing centre. As the only legal outlet for a flutter in the gambling-mad territory, the Jockey Club, which has a monopoly on the sport, had a turnover of more than HK$80 billion (US$11 billion) in 1995.
